chunks: Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbbād, from Kathīr al-Nawwāʾ, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the major sins, and he said: "Every sin for which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has threatened the Fire."

key_terms.أَوْعَدَ: threatened or warned of punishment for
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the Divine Lawgiver and Judge
key_terms.النَّارَ: the Hellfire; the punishment of the afterlife
key_terms.الْكَبَائِرِ: the major sins; grave acts of disobedience
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: the Mighty and Majestic; an honorific for Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام define the major sins in hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith defines major sins by a clear criterion: any act for which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has threatened the Hellfire counts as a major sin. It highlights the gravity of sins tied to divine warning and connects moral wrongdoing directly to accountability in the afterlife.
